title.hi: Drivers aur trips ko join karte hain
title.te: Drivers mariyu trips ni join cheddam

en: SELECT → defines which columns will be shown in output.
d.driver_id → driver id from drivers table.
d.driver_name → driver name from drivers table.
d.city → city from drivers table.
t.fare → fare from trips table.
FROM drivers d → drivers is main table, alias 'd' is used for short reference.
JOIN trips t → joining second table trips with alias 't'.
ON d.driver_id = t.driver_id → join condition, matching both tables.
Only matching records between drivers and trips will be returned.
ta: SELECT → output-la varanum columns decide pannum.
d.driver_id → drivers table-lendhu driver id.
d.driver_name → driver name.
d.city → driver city.
t.fare → trips table-lendhu fare.
FROM drivers d → main table, 'd' nu alias kuduthom.
JOIN trips t → trips table join pannrom, 't' nu alias.
ON d.driver_id = t.driver_id → rendu table connect aagum condition.
Match aana rows dhaan result-la varum.

te: SELECT → output lo ye columns chupinchalo decide chestundi.
d.driver_id → drivers table nundi id.
d.driver_name → driver peru.
d.city → driver city.
t.fare → trips table nundi fare.
FROM drivers d → main table, 'd' alias.

steps.sql:
SELECT d.driver_id,
       d.driver_name,
       d.city,
       SUM(t.fare) AS total_earnings
FROM drivers d
JOIN trips t ON d.driver_id = t.driver_id
GROUP BY d.driver_id, d.driver_name, d.city
ORDER BY total_earnings DESC;

en: SUM(t.fare) → adds all fares for each driver.
AS total_earnings → gives a readable name to result column.
GROUP BY d.driver_id → groups data per driver.
GROUP BY d.driver_name, d.city → ensures proper grouping without SQL error.
Each driver will have one row after grouping.
ORDER BY total_earnings DESC → sorts from highest earning to lowest.

AS total_earnings → column-ku peru kudukkrom.
GROUP BY driver_id → driver-wise group pannum.
driver_name, city add pannradhu SQL error avoid panna.
Oru driver-ku oru row dhaan varum.
ORDER BY DESC → highest earning mudhal varum.
hi: SUM(t.fare) → har driver ke saare fares add karta hai.
AS total_earnings → column ka naam set karta hai.
GROUP BY driver_id → driver ke hisaab se grouping.
driver_name, city bhi include karna zaroori hai.
Har driver ka ek hi row aayega.
ORDER BY DESC → highest earning pehle.

title.hi: Har city ke top 3 drivers nikalte hain
title.te: Prathi city lo top 3 drivers kanukundam

steps.sql:
SELECT driver_id, driver_name, city, total_earnings
FROM (
  SELECT d.driver_id,
         d.driver_name,
         d.city,
         SUM(t.fare) AS total_earnings,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY d.city
           ORDER BY SUM(t.fare) DESC
         ) AS rn
  FROM drivers d
  JOIN trips t ON d.driver_id = t.driver_id
  GROUP BY d.driver_id, d.driver_name, d.city
) ranked
WHERE rn <= 3;

en: ROW_NUMBER() → assigns ranking number.
OVER() → defines window function behavior.
PARTITION BY d.city → resets ranking for each city.
ORDER BY SUM(fare) DESC → highest earning gets rank 1.
Subquery → needed because we filter using rn.
WHERE rn <= 3 → selects top 3 drivers per city.
ta: ROW_NUMBER() → rank number kudukkum.
OVER() → window function epdi work aagum nu define pannum.
PARTITION BY city → ovvoru city-kum separate ranking.
ORDER BY DESC → highest earner rank 1.
Subquery → first ranking calculate panna use pannrom.
WHERE rn <= 3 → top 3 mattum edukkrom.
hi: ROW_NUMBER() → ranking deta hai.
OVER() → window function ka behavior define karta hai.
PARTITION BY city → har city ke liye alag ranking.
ORDER BY DESC → highest earning rank 1.
Subquery → pehle ranking calculate karna zaroori hai.
WHERE rn <= 3 → top 3 drivers select.
te: ROW_NUMBER() → ranking number istundi.
OVER() → window function ela pani chestundo define chestundi.
PARTITION BY city → prathi city ki separate ranking.
ORDER BY DESC → highest ki rank 1.

WHERE rn <= 3 → top 3 drivers select chestam.
